title: Booking & availability
summary: Reserve shared resources with explicit time zones, overlap rules, expiring holds, and cancellation policies.
outcome: A booking app that handles competing requests, time boundaries, rescheduling, and reminder delivery without double booking.
prerequisites: Shared projects, inventory concurrency, and deterministic clocks. Begin with one resource type and a small explicit booking policy.
model: Resource: id, ownerId, name, capacity, timeZone, active. Booking: resourceId, startsAt, endsAt, status, revision.
Hold: booking intent, expiry, operationId. AvailabilityRule: local weekday/time ranges and explicit exceptions.
Use half-open intervals [start, end) unless the product defines another boundary. Display zone and stored instants serve different purposes.
boundaries: Local-time input → explicit zone resolution → booking service → concurrency-safe storage. Reminder work is delivered through an outbox.

milestones.title: Create resources and opening hours
milestones.brief: Build resource CRUD and weekly availability rules with explicit ownership, capacity, and exception dates.
milestones.explanation: Opening hours are local calendar rules, while a confirmed booking usually refers to specific instants. Keep those representations distinct. Define whether overnight hours are supported and how exceptions override the weekly schedule. Resource archival must have a declared effect on future bookings rather than silently deleting customer commitments.
steps: Write examples for a closed day, an overnight range, an exception date, and resource archival. Define the supported capacity model.
Implement resource and availability-rule CRUD with validated time-zone identifiers and range boundaries. Scope every write to an authorized owner.
Display a human-readable weekly schedule and test keyboard editing, duplicate rules, and reload persistence.

checks.label: Availability rules reject impossible or unsupported ranges.
Exception dates follow the documented precedence.
Resource archival preserves existing booking history.

milestones.experiment: Create an exception on a normally open day and an opening on a normally closed day. Verify the schedule reflects the explicit override rule.
milestones.review: Ask the agent to explain why a local recurring opening time cannot be represented by one fixed UTC offset for the entire year.
milestones.stretch: Add an availability preview for a selected week without creating booking records.

milestones.title: Resolve local times explicitly
milestones.brief: Convert selected local booking times into instants while handling nonexistent and repeated times at daylight-saving transitions.
milestones.explanation: Some local clock times occur twice and others do not occur at all. A date, time, and time-zone identifier may therefore need a disambiguation policy. Validate the resolved interval, show the chosen zone to the user, and avoid silently interpreting input in the server's or browser's unrelated default zone.
steps: Create fixtures around a forward and backward clock change in one supported zone, plus a zone without seasonal changes.
Implement explicit local-time resolution using the chosen time library and its documented disambiguation behavior. Reject or ask for clarification on ambiguous input according to your policy.
Round-trip stored instants to the displayed zone and test changing the viewer's zone without changing the booking itself.

checks.label: Nonexistent and ambiguous times follow an explicit tested policy.
Stored duration and ordering remain correct across zone changes.
The confirmation clearly identifies the booking's displayed time zone.

milestones.experiment: Choose a local time that occurs twice and submit both possible offsets. Verify they are treated as different instants rather than accidental duplicates.
milestones.review: Document whether duration is elapsed time or wall-clock time. Do not hand-roll time-zone offset tables or assume every day lasts exactly 24 hours.
milestones.stretch: Add a display showing the resource's zone and the customer's zone side by side.

milestones.title: Reject conflicting reservations atomically
milestones.brief: Prevent two clients from committing overlapping reservations for the same exclusive resource.
milestones.explanation: Checking availability and later inserting a booking creates a race. Enforce the overlap rule at the database boundary using a suitable constraint or locking strategy. Adjacent intervals can be allowed under half-open semantics, but zero-length, reversed, and out-of-hours intervals still need separate validation.
steps: Specify overlap examples, including exact adjacency, full containment, and identical intervals. Begin with capacity one before generalizing.
Implement the protected insert and map conflict into a typed domain error. Keep the selected form values so the user can choose another time.
Launch simultaneous overlapping requests against the real database and inspect committed rows. Test a rollback after a booking-related write fails.

checks.label: Only one conflicting request commits for an exclusive resource.
Invalid or failed requests leave no partial booking records.

milestones.experiment: Pause both requests after their availability read, then release them together. A correct implementation must still protect the invariant at commit.
milestones.review: Show the constraint or lock that survives multiple API instances. A disabled browser button or process-local lock does not cover this race.
milestones.stretch: Extend the model to capacity greater than one and explain why the exclusive-resource solution alone is insufficient.

milestones.title: Manage expiring temporary holds
milestones.brief: Hold availability briefly while a user confirms, then finalize or expire the hold exactly once.
milestones.explanation: A hold is a temporary state with an expiry rule, not a confirmed booking. Confirmation and expiration may compete. Protect the transition and resource accounting in one transaction, and derive the authoritative expiry decision from a trusted clock. A client countdown is only a display of that server policy.
steps: Define hold creation, extension if allowed, confirmation, and expiry. Set a maximum lifetime and a policy for repeated requests.
Implement a conditional state transition and an expiry worker with bounded batches. Return an established result when the same confirmation command is retried.
Test just-before, exactly-at, and just-after expiry using a controllable clock, including a worker restart.

checks.label: Expired holds cannot be confirmed under the declared boundary rule.
Confirmation and expiry cannot both apply resource accounting.
A repeated command returns a consistent result without extra reservations.

milestones.experiment: Race confirmation against the expiry worker at the same timestamp. Inspect both responses and the final hold and booking states.
milestones.review: Explain which clock is authoritative and what happens when a worker runs late. Availability must not rely solely on a perfectly punctual background timer.
milestones.stretch: Add a diagnostic showing expired-but-not-yet-cleaned holds without treating them as active capacity.

milestones.title: Reschedule without losing the old booking
milestones.brief: Move a booking to a new interval while preserving the original reservation if the replacement cannot be accepted.
milestones.explanation: Rescheduling is not safely implemented as an unconditional delete followed by create. Validate current permission and revision, reserve the replacement under the same concurrency rule, and release the old allocation inside one transaction where the storage model permits it. External side effects belong after the committed change.
steps: Define who can reschedule and cancel, which time cutoffs apply, and how archived resources affect existing bookings.
Implement revision-aware reschedule and cancellation commands. Preserve old state on conflict and show both requested and current values for recovery.
Test an occupied destination, simultaneous cancellations, and two competing reschedules from one revision. Inspect history as well as availability.

checks.label: A rejected reschedule preserves the original booking.
Accepted changes update availability and history consistently.
Stale or repeated actions cannot release capacity twice.

milestones.experiment: Attempt to move a booking into an interval another client reserves concurrently. Verify the losing request retains its old reservation.
milestones.review: Check cancellation and rescheduling policies at the service boundary. UI date pickers can guide valid choices but cannot enforce a cutoff against direct requests.
milestones.stretch: Add a waitlist promotion operation and prove that two workers cannot promote the same vacancy twice.

milestones.title: Deliver reminders after committed changes
milestones.brief: Send reminders for current bookings and suppress jobs made obsolete by cancellation or rescheduling.
milestones.explanation: A queued reminder describes a future action based on a past state. Recheck the current booking version before delivery, and distinguish an obsolete job from a transient provider failure. Commit the scheduling intent with the booking change, then let a separate worker deliver it with bounded retries and duplicate protection.
steps: Model reminder identity, booking revision, scheduled time, attempt state, and delivery outcome. Define how rescheduling invalidates older jobs.
Add outbox creation to the booking transaction and a worker that checks current status before contacting a fake provider.
Test cancellation after queueing, rescheduling during a delayed attempt, a lost provider response, and worker restart.

checks.label: Only eligible current bookings produce reminders.
Obsolete jobs are recorded without sending stale details.
Retries and restarts respect the declared duplicate-delivery policy.

milestones.experiment: Queue a reminder, cancel the booking, then release the paused worker. Verify it observes cancellation before sending.
milestones.review: A local receipt cannot prove whether an external provider accepted a timed-out request. Document the provider's idempotency support and remaining ambiguity.
milestones.stretch: Deploy the app, restore a backup into a test environment, and ensure restored jobs cannot accidentally send real reminders.
